note: F2: The house answer must not promise outcomes Fairtrade says its standards cannot ensure alone.

expect:
Top band (5-6): Thorough discussion. E.g., 3D printing does not require a mould, so setup costs are low, but each unit takes time to print and finish — suitable for small batches only. Injection moulding requires an expensive steel mould (high setup cost) but produces each unit in seconds with excellent consistency and surface finish. For 500 units, injection moulding is more cost-effective overall because the per-unit cost drops sharply once the mould is made. 3D printing would only be preferable for very small quantities or complex geometries that cannot be moulded.
Mid band (3-4): Adequate discussion with some comparison.
Lower band (1-2): Basic identification of one method with limited justification.
value:
Top band (5-6): Thorough discussion. E.g., 3D printing does not require a mould, so setup costs are low, but each unit takes time to print and finish — suitable for small batches only. Injection moulding requires a mould with an upfront setup cost but produces each unit in seconds with excellent consistency and surface finish. At 500 units, the most cost-effective process depends on the part design, tooling and supplier costs. 3D printing may be preferable for very small quantities or complex geometries that cannot be moulded.
Mid band (3-4): Adequate discussion with some comparison.
Lower band (1-2): Basic identification of one method with limited justification.
note: F6: Injection moulding can use aluminium tooling; a 500-unit break-even point cannot be assumed.

value: Computer Numerical Control — computer control of a machine tool using programmed numerical instructions.
note: F7: CNC is a control method; routing and milling are subtractive CNC operations.
